A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DC research despite the shortened title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original counting experiments on 100 synthetic and 20 real scenes, occupancy-estimation results, depth-map ablations, and a supplementary border-effects analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original synthetic experiments and reports evaluation on 45 real scenes, human estimates from 33 participants, additional computational comparisons, and new ablation and complexity results.

M1.justification: v2's main method replaces alpha-concave-hull volume estimation and user-specified thickness with mask/depth-based voxel carving and erosion using a learned thickness decoder. It also introduces automatic key-view selection by object-mask area and exemplar reconstruction for unknown unit volumes. The occupancy network's basic architecture remains. These substantially revise inference, although the appendix retains the earlier alpha-hull implementation description.

E1.justification: Synthetic coverage expands from filled, fixed-box simulations to containers with varying shapes and scales, partially filled containers, and container-free piles, explicitly described in v2 Sec. 3.2 and illustrated in Fig. 5. These broaden the represented training environments beyond merely increasing sample counts.

E2.justification: v2 adds CNN and ViT+H direct-count regressors to Tables 1–2, and Human, Human-Vote, and LlamaVision 3.2 comparisons to real-scene Table 2. BMNet+, SAM+CLIP, and the three occupancy-estimation baselines remain. The added comparator families substantially broaden the evaluation.

E3.justification: Real evaluation expands from 20 to 45 scenes, and the reported manual-counting versus weight-based ground-truth cutoff changes from 1000 to 500 objects. v2 reports 4800 synthetic shapes and about 14000 scenes, replacing v1's over-2500-shapes description. It introduces a 33-participant, 1485-estimate human evaluation and a shape-complexity evaluation measure. The synthetic test size and existing error-metric formulas remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an RGB-versus-depth input ablation, quantitative occupancy-error analysis against shape complexity, and discussion of human performance versus effort and guessing strategy. These test additional design and robustness questions. The original depth-map ablations and supplementary border-effects analysis remain; the dedicated rice partial-view demonstration disappears, and qualitative complex-shape failures give way to the quantitative complexity analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new participant averages define human comparison methods; they do not introduce uncertainty estimates or repeated-training-run reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the 20-scene results, including 3DC NAE 0.15 and sMAPE 34.20, with 45-scene results of 0.36 and 53.31, alongside new comparator and RGB-ablation scores. These are changed-setting results, not evidence of same-setting deterioration. Retained Table 1 rows and Tables 3–5 preserve their numerical values. Qualitative estimates also change: pasta is estimated as 2025 in v1 and 509 in v2, against ground truth 588.

T1.justification: v2 Sec. 4.5 introduces a mathematical shape-complexity definition combining normalized integrated mean curvature and convex-hull volume deficit. The principal counting equation and existing evaluation formulas remain unchanged; moving metric formulas into the supplement adds no new theory. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Although the abstract and two-part counting contribution remain, v2 adds a human benchmark to its stated contributions and claims substantial superiority over humans. Its introduction also argues that direct single-step prediction may be infeasible and decomposition is critical, extending v1's claim that decomposition provides an effective solution.

C2.justification: v1 describes little synthetic-to-real performance variation; v2 acknowledges weaker real-scene performance and attributes it to scene complexity and volume estimation. It adds interpretations of human guessing and an explicit depth-based domain-gap explanation. Complex-shape limitations are reframed around a slight quantitative error increase. The explicit user-selection limitation disappears even though initial segmentation remains required.

D1.justification: v2 documents thickness-target normalization, supervision, averaging across views, and exemplar reconstruction. It omits v1's training crop/flip and masked-pixel random-supervision disclosures, and no longer states the planned network-weight release. Most backbone, image-resolution, and hardware details remain. The appendix's retained alpha-hull implementation description is not reconciled with the revised main method.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Edelsbrunner et al. alpha-shape reference and adds Multi-scale Context Aggregation by Dilated Convolutions. Positioning against single-view counting, multi-view counting, and LiDAR-based CountNet3D remains substantially unchanged. Most other bibliography edits concern the same cited works.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the introduction, method exposition, and conclusion; places occupancy estimation before volume estimation; integrates dataset generation into the occupancy section; and moves metric formulas into a dedicated supplementary section. It also shortens the title and standardizes occupancy-ratio terminology. This reorganizes substantial existing material.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the pipeline, replaces numerous example panels, adds domain-gap and complexity visualizations, and redesigns the intermediate-results display around three examples and reconstructed exemplars. Tables 1–2 gain rows and metric-direction indicators. The supplementary scene gallery is removed, while the existing dataset-statistics figure moves from the main text to the supplement.

improvement.justification: The direct-count baselines, RGB ablation, and quantitative complexity analysis provide better evidence for the design choices than v1's comparisons alone. The expanded real evaluation also leads to a more qualified generalization discussion. These benefits outweigh the documentation losses, but the unreconciled alpha-hull appendix versus voxel-carving main method and omitted implementation disclosures limit the net gain. The changed real test set does not establish a performance improvement.
